scenarios.title: A first deploy
scenarios.intro: A Node.js API and its Postgres database, as first put on a Linux server.
scenarios.label: compose.yaml

scenarios.title: Almost ready for a server
scenarios.intro: The same app a few weeks later. Someone has added a volume and a healthcheck.
scenarios.label: compose.yaml

questions.prompt: Your Dockerfile starts with `FROM node:latest`. What is the problem?
options: It is the smallest Node image
Docker refuses to build it
The same Dockerfile can build a different Node version next month
It only works on Apple Silicon
questions.explanation: `latest` is whatever was newest on the day you build. Pin a version such as `node:24-alpine`, so every build gets the Node you tested with.

questions.prompt: You wrote `ENV API_KEY=sk-live-123` in a Dockerfile and pushed the image. Who can read the key?
options: Anyone who can pull the image
Only the app inside the container
Nobody: ENV values are encrypted
Only the person who built it
questions.explanation: ENV values are saved in the image. `docker history` and `docker image inspect` show them. Pass secrets in when the container starts instead.

questions.prompt: `docker stop` pauses for a few seconds, and the container then shows `Exited (137)`. What happened?
options: The app finished cleanly
The port was already in use
The image was built for another CPU
The app ignored the stop signal, so Docker killed it
questions.explanation: 137 means killed. Node running as process 1 ignores SIGTERM unless the code handles it. Add a `process.on('SIGTERM', ...)` handler, or run with `--init`.

questions.prompt: You ran the app with `-p 8084:3000`. The log says it is listening, but `localhost:8084` does not load. The app calls `app.listen(3000, '127.0.0.1')`. Why does it fail?
options: Port 8084 is reserved by Docker
Inside the container, 127.0.0.1 is the container itself, and traffic from -p does not arrive there
Node cannot listen inside a container
The browser blocks port 8084
questions.explanation: Published traffic arrives on the container's network address. Listen on `0.0.0.0` inside the container, and limit who can reach it with the `-p` side instead.

questions.prompt: With `volumes: [./:/app]` the app says Cannot find package 'express', although the image installed it. Why?
options: npm install failed without telling you
express is a devDependency
The bind mount covers all of /app, including the image's node_modules
Compose ignores the Dockerfile when volumes are set
questions.explanation: A bind mount lays your folder over the path. Your folder has no node_modules, so neither does the container. An extra `- /app/node_modules` volume keeps the image's copy.

questions.prompt: An image built on an Apple Silicon Mac fails on the server with `exec format error`. What fixes it?
options: Build it with `--platform linux/amd64`, or build it in CI
Run it with `--init`
Publish a different port
Switch the base image to `node:latest`
questions.explanation: The image was built for arm64 and the server is amd64. Build for the server's CPU.

questions.prompt: What does a plain `depends_on: [db]` guarantee?
options: The database accepts connections before the app starts
The app restarts when the database restarts
Both services share one volume
The db container is started before the app container
questions.explanation: Started is not ready. A new Postgres takes a few seconds to set itself up. Use a healthcheck with `condition: service_healthy` to wait for ready.

questions.context: The key should reach the app when the container starts, and never be saved in the image.
questions.prompt: Fill in the flag.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: `-e` sets an environment variable for this one container. The image stays free of the key.

questions.context: You want the app on port 8084, reachable from your own machine only, not from the rest of the network. The app listens on port 3000.
questions.prompt: Fill in the port mapping.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: Putting `127.0.0.1` in front publishes on the loopback address only. Plain `8084:3000` opens it on every network, and on Linux it gets past ufw too.

questions.context: The db service has a healthcheck. The app should wait until it passes.
questions.prompt: Fill in the condition.
questions.label: compose.yaml
questions.explanation: `service_healthy` waits for the healthcheck to pass. The default, `service_started`, only waits for the container to start.

questions.context: In development you bind-mount the project folder over /app, but the packages the image installed must stay visible.
questions.prompt: Fill in the second volume.
questions.label: compose.yaml
questions.explanation: A volume on the more specific path wins over the bind mount, so /app/node_modules keeps the image's packages.

questions.context: You are on an Apple Silicon Mac, and the server is an ordinary amd64 machine.
questions.prompt: Fill in the flag.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: `--platform` picks the CPU the image is built for. Check it afterwards with `docker image inspect --format '{{.Architecture}}'`.

questions.prompt: The server's firewall (ufw) blocks port 5432. Can someone on the internet reach this database?
options: No: ufw blocks it
Only if they know the password
Only from the same Docker network
Yes: Docker's published ports get past ufw, so remove the db's ports
questions.explanation: Docker writes its own firewall rules for published ports. The api reaches db over the Compose network, so db needs no `ports` at all.

questions.prompt: The api exits with `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432`. What is the fix?
options: Set `PGHOST: db`
Publish 5432 on the api too
Add `restart: always` to the api
Use `postgres:17` instead of latest
questions.explanation: localhost inside the api container is the api container. Compose gives each service a DNS name, so the database is `db`.

questions.prompt: After `docker compose down` and `up` again, every table is gone. Why?
options: down always deletes data
Postgres forgets its data when the password is short
db has no volume, so the data lived in the container that down removed
The api dropped the tables on start
questions.explanation: Without a volume on /var/lib/postgresql/data, the data is part of the container. Add a named volume, as in the second file.

questions.prompt: Nothing in the file changed, but after the server pulled images again the database will not start. What in this file is the likely cause?
options: `build: .` on the api
`image: postgres:latest` jumped to a new major version
`POSTGRES_PASSWORD` is too short
depends_on is in the wrong order
questions.explanation: A new Postgres major version cannot read an older one's data files without an upgrade. Pin the version, for example `postgres:17-alpine`.

questions.prompt: db has a healthcheck, but on a fresh server web still crashes the first time. What is missing?
options: A volume on web
A second healthcheck on web
`condition: service_healthy` under web's depends_on
A published port on db
questions.explanation: A healthcheck only reports. Nothing waits for it until depends_on asks for `condition: service_healthy`.

questions.prompt: Who can open web on port 8084?
options: Only programs on the server itself
Anyone on the internet
Anyone on the same network
Nobody, until you open it in the firewall
questions.explanation: `127.0.0.1:8084:3000` publishes on the loopback address only. A reverse proxy or tunnel on the server then decides what the outside can see.

questions.prompt: The server reboots for updates, and afterwards nothing is running. What would bring both services back on their own?
options: A healthcheck on web
`restart: unless-stopped` on both services
A bigger volume
Running `docker compose up` without -d
questions.explanation: Without a restart policy, Docker leaves containers stopped after a reboot. `unless-stopped` starts them again, unless you stopped them yourself.

questions.prompt: Months later, the server's disk is full. What in this file allows that?
options: The healthcheck runs too often
The shopdata volume has no size
web publishes a port
No logging limits: the default log file never rotates
questions.explanation: The default json-file log driver keeps every line for ever. Add `logging.options` with `max-size` and `max-file`, and check with `docker system df`.
